## Qualified and published — 2026-10-08

All121 bundled ELF/plugin closures resolve with the required project-target libcom-err. Normal isolated target build/install passed; x64 architecture, SONAME, six installed outputs and protected-input hashes are verified. Actual native rendering/capture succeeds; no host library or accepted build-root mutation was used.

Product integration `e6645cb5ea5ae3c7f699390a74b22d098fbeb7fb` and [retained proof](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-08-save-repair-cases) are published on next `bc4ae05d30531516ebd19b6b167fc994f368c4c3`; ES integration is `4e410dc9a816cc947f16235ad2b24824b29dd84e`. The independent delta audit (#507), assembled firmware inclusion/public adoption (#508), affected device builds and release gates remain separate. #519 must pass before the owner's next handheld update transfer/reboot. No personal cloud or physical action was part of this qualification.

The sections below retain the problem, requirement and investigation history; this status supersedes their earlier in-progress observations.

## Problem and placement

Actual #521/#522 GENERIC_X64 proof now reaches the pinned DuckStation loader with correct executable mode, then fails because a required shared library is absent. Track the complete required runtime dependency closure here before retrying screenshot proof, rather than recording permission repair as successful application startup.

## Code trace

- Qualified guest overlay keeps the exact pinned x64 AppImage SHA256 `b204886bb498ede1a290215fc2efb521c0c2f26b964788df697b4fc2cb3f7f7b`, mode0755. Direct entrypoint reports `error while loading shared libraries: libcom_err.so.2` and exits127. No emulator session/capture started.
- DuckStation's recipe declares toolchain (plus the new screenshot helper's Python3 dependency) but not the required `libcom-err` package. Existing `projects/ROCKNIX/packages/devel/libcom-err/package.mk:40–44` installs that library; another standalone recipe already declares it.
- Verify the actual AppImage runtime/ELF closure, add required existing packages explicitly and prove the package/image installs their real target artifacts. No host-library copying or bundled-byte modification is a product fix.
- Already written: images can contain an intact application that fails loader startup; persistent progress and screenshots need no repair because of this loader failure. Keep packaged artifact identity and existing configuration; new assembled firmware must include the qualified dependency closure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Original actual-guest failure, exact artifact and loader dependency/source trace are retained, separating executable permission from loader readiness.
- [x] Recipe declares the required runtime closure using project packages; pkgcheck and target package/install evidence prove library bytes/architecture/SONAME and placement. Existing frozen build owners and global source caches are unchanged.
- [x] Actual owned GENERIC_X64 proof starts the real AppImage with the qualified target libraries and no missing required dependencies; #521's screenshot writer proof resumes on that exact overlay. Any unrelated runtime restriction is named, not silently passed.
- [x] #508 integration/#507 audit/final firmware inclusion manifest name the dependency inputs and preserve separate source-overlay versus assembled-image qualification.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. Inspect the real pinned artifact and target loader, build/install any required package in a named isolated source owner if necessary, and use the existing disposable guest. No private data, device action, second guest or host-system library installation is required. Long work uses the watcher and active result delivery.
